To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
LRIG1 is a novel regulator of EGFR activity in lung epithelial cells.
Loss of contact inhibition in lung epithelia is regulated by LRIG1 and is a key step in the development of lung cancer.
LRIG1 is a novel regulator of contact inhibition and that loss of LRIG1 expression is a frequent event early in human squamous lung carcinogenesis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
identifying the molecular mechanism of LRIG1 mediated control of EGFR activity and its role in the initiation and progression of preinvasive and invasive squamous lung cancer.
the mechanisms by which the EGFR pathway is regulated in vivo and the role of this regulation in human lung cancer.
the mechanisms that govern tissue homeostasis, the loss of which is a critical step in the initiation and progression of lung cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
LRIG1 is an essential regulator of contact inhibition and its loss is an initiating event in lung cancer development.
LRIG1 is a key regulator of epithelial homeostatis and preinvasive lung cancer development.
LRIG1 is a key regulator of EGFR activity in normal and neoplastic lung cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
LRIG1 acts as a tumor suppressor gene that regulates EGFR signaling and cell contact inhibition in the airway epithelium.
LRIG1 regulates cell adhesion, growth and EGFR signaling.
LRIG1 regulates epithelial homeostatic mechanisms and its loss promotes the initiation of preneoplastic lung disease.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the LRIG1-EGFR interaction is a key mechanism for regulating epithelial cell growth and homeostasis.
LRIG1 is a key negative regulator of epithelial homeostatic control of EGFR signaling and that loss of this control is a critical event in the development of lung cancer.
LRIG1 regulates the amplitude of EGFG signaling and its loss is a driver of preinvasive disease.
